idiom_name: virtual-interface proxy chain (std::unique_ptr<Service>) or a std::function pipeline
implementation_notes: C++ realises the pattern with the classic structure: an abstract Service interface, one proxy class per gate holding a std::unique_ptr to the next gate, and a call that checks first and then delegates, so gates nest by construction (make_unique<InnerGate>(make_unique<OuterGate>(service))). What replaces the classic structure: std::function and lambdas let the gates be plain callables instead of classes, and std::unique_ptr keeps ownership of the chain unambiguous, so the function-object form is the lighter idiom; the class form is still justified when a gate holds configuration, needs virtual dispatch or must be replaced at runtime.
pitfalls: A gate that caches a verified identity or holds mutable session state leaks privileges across requests unless that state is per-request or explicitly synchronised.
Chain ownership must be explicit: passing a reference to a stack-allocated gate that outlives the call dangles, and unique_ptr chains cannot be copied.
An exception thrown by a gate or by the resource unwinds through the chain; error paths need the same deny semantics as the check itself, or a failure of the gate becomes an allow.
